newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's PTTEP details increased reserves.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's PTTEP details increased reserves.

text.p: Reserves of Thailand's state-backed oil company PTT Exploration and Production Plc rose over the last six months, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
Proven reserves are 553.2 million barrels of oil or equivalent (mmboe) as of June 30. The figure is a 10.2 percent increase from figures released at the end of 1996.
Probable and possible reserves are 663.2 mmboe, the statement added.
Total remaining proven reserves comprised of 3.5 trillion cubic feet (tcf) of gas and 50.5 million barrels (mmbbl) of crude oil and condensate, the firm said.
The increase in proven reserves was due to appraisals of the company's Yetagun project off the Burmese coast, and improved recovery from the Bongkot Field in the Gulf of Thailand, it said.
The probable and possible reserves consisted of 3.8 tcf of natural gas and 70.4 mmbbl of oil and condensate, it addded.

A 25.7 percent increase in probable and possible reserves to 663.2 mmboe over the last six months was also due to reassessment of the company's Yetagun Project and North Paillin Gulf project in block B12/27, the company said.
The 663.2 mmboe total is still 23 percent less than the 870 mmboe probable and possible reserves figure announced in June 1996.
In February PTTEP announced a 342 mmboe decline in possible and probable reserves over the six months from June to December last year.
Production in the first six months of 1997 averaged 40,000 barrels per day, the company said.
